newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMP Society year net profit rises to A$2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: AMP Society year net profit rises to A$2.1 bln.

text.p: The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Monday that its calendar 1996 net profit rose to A$2.1 billion from A$1.9 billion.
AMP total income fell slightly at A$16 billion in 1996 from A$18 billion in 1995, reflecting lower movement in the investment markets.

"While we are not yet satisfied with the operating performance and returns in our major businesses, 1996 did continue the positive trend toward our established operating targets," AMP managing director George Trumbull said in a statement.
Sales for single premium business were up 27 percent across the group in 1997 and five percent for regular premiums.

"AMP made good progress in 1996 and continues the evolution commenced two years ago. We can see progress being made across the company and we can measure the impact this progress is having on our operations," Trumbull said. AMP said its unit trust sales were also up four-fold on the 1995 results.
"This improvement in sales was achieved in Australia and the United Kingdom where both the retail businesses benefitted from restructuring," the company said in a statement.
AMP said its life business in New Zealand also lifted total premium income to A$7.4 billion compared with A$7.0 billion in 1995.

AMP said its investment in Pearl Assurance in the U.K. benefitted from an improved performance and particularly from an abnormal profit associated with the agreement with the regulator in the U.K. that a substantial part of the Pearl orphan estate was clearly attributable to the shareholder.
Pearl policy holdings also beneifted from the estate through the payment of a special bonus totalling A$630 million, AMP said.
AMP said total operating expenses in AMP were contained to 1995 levels at A$2.4 billion across all business units.
"AMP's inherent capital strength is increasing due to good recent results," Trumbull said.
Retained profits for members and policy owners amounted to A$9.1 billion.
"AMP is working on a number of fronts to improve the operational efficiency and the profitability of the company," he said.
AMP has said it plans to demutualise and listing on the Austraian Exchange towards the end of 1998.
